dancers.name: Jenna Dewan
dancers.knownFor: The Rookie • Step Up • actor and dancer
dancers.danceBackground: Elite — former professional backup dancer for Janet Jackson, Missy Elliott and others
dancers.bio: Jenna first won over dance-movie fans in Step Up and now stars on The Rookie. She spent years dancing professionally behind artists like Janet Jackson and Missy Elliott, so she should look comfortable from the very first count. With Val beside her, this pairing has polish, chemistry potential and very high expectations.
dancers.preseasonUpdate: The early prediction market has her narrowly on top at about 20%. Her professional dance résumé raises the ceiling, while possible voter resistance to a perceived advantage remains the main risk.

dancers.name: Harry Shum Jr.
dancers.danceBackground: Elite — professional dancer, choreographer and former backup dancer
dancers.bio: Harry is beloved from Glee, the Step Up films, Shadowhunters and Grey's Anatomy. Dance has been part of his career for years, including performances with Beyoncé and Jennifer Lopez, but ballroom brings a completely different kind of posture and partnership. Jenna Johnson should have plenty of creativity to work with here.
dancers.preseasonUpdate: Running near the top of the early prediction market at about 18%. Harry says ballroom technique feels distinctly different from his prior professional dance work, so hold and frame will be the first real test.

dancers.name: Amber Glenn
dancers.danceBackground: Strong crossover — elite musicality, edges, spins, lines and performance from figure skating
dancers.bio: Amber is a champion figure skater who knows exactly how to perform when the lights come on. Her musicality, beautiful lines and ability to tell a story on the ice could translate wonderfully to the ballroom. Watching Pasha turn that skating confidence into true partner dancing should be one of the season's most interesting journeys.
dancers.preseasonUpdate: An early top-tier contender at about 18% in the prediction market. Her elite skating background is translating into strong preseason confidence before the first scored dance.

dancers.name: Julia Stiles
dancers.knownFor: 10 Things I Hate About You • Save the Last Dance
dancers.danceBackground: Moderate — intensive ballet and hip-hop preparation for Save the Last Dance
dancers.bio: Julia will always be a favorite for 10 Things I Hate About You and Save the Last Dance. She trained seriously for that famous dance role, but has been open about how long it has been since she danced that way—and even felt nervous stepping into heels again. That makes her partnership with Ezra feel less like a sure thing and more like a lovely comeback story.
dancers.preseasonUpdate: Julia clarified that she stopped formal dance after Save the Last Dance and entered rehearsals nervous about dancing in heels. Ezra has praised her dedication; treat the movie résumé as useful familiarity, not current professional training.

dancers.name: Ciara Miller
dancers.knownFor: Summer House • model • former travel nurse
dancers.danceBackground: Strong foundation — about 10 years of ballet growing up
dancers.bio: Summer House fans know Ciara for her cool confidence, quick wit and effortless style. She also spent many childhood years in ballet, which could give her a head start with posture, lines and body awareness. Brandon has a partner who already knows how to command a camera; now we get to see how quickly the ballroom side clicks.

dancers.name: Maura Higgins
dancers.knownFor: Love Island UK • The Traitors • TV presenter
dancers.danceBackground: Moderate — childhood Irish dancing plus Dancing on Ice choreography
dancers.bio: Maura became a fan favorite on Love Island UK thanks to her humor, honesty and huge personality. She danced as a child and has already handled choreographed performance on Dancing on Ice, so she should not be shy about throwing herself into a routine. Pairing her with the wonderfully inventive Mark Ballas feels like a recipe for memorable television.

dancers.name: Tyler Cameron
dancers.danceBackground: Some crossover — competed on The Real Dirty Dancing; former college football player
dancers.bio: Tyler became one of Bachelor Nation's most popular contestants after The Bachelorette, and he has since taken on everything from modeling to Special Forces. His football background gives him athleticism, while The Real Dirty Dancing gave him a taste of partner choreography. Sharna's return makes this an especially easy pairing to root for.

dancers.name: Ezra Frech
dancers.danceBackground: No formal training established — elite explosiveness, balance and body control
dancers.bio: Ezra is a Paralympic champion, disability advocate and deeply competitive athlete who has spent his life finding creative ways to excel. Ballroom is brand-new territory, but confidence, body control and fearlessness are already part of who he is. Daniella is one of the show's boldest choreographers, so this could become a genuinely special partnership.
dancers.preseasonUpdate: His early prediction-market chance has climbed to roughly 15%, placing him just behind the three preseason leaders. Athletic upside and Daniella's choreography are driving the rise.

dancers.name: Tatyana Ali
dancers.knownFor: The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air • actor and singer
dancers.danceBackground: Performance background — Broadway-trained actor and recording artist; no ballroom record
dancers.bio: Tatyana grew up on television as Ashley Banks on The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air and is also a singer, producer and Harvard graduate. She brings warmth, musical instincts and years of stage experience, even if ballroom itself is new. Her partnership with Jan has the potential to be charming, joyful and full of personality.

dancers.name: Taylor Hanson
dancers.danceBackground: Performance crossover — lifelong musician with strong rhythm; no formal training established
dancers.bio: Taylor has spent most of his life making music and performing for live audiences as part of Hanson. He may be new to ballroom, but rhythm, stamina and connecting with a crowd are already second nature. Britt is a patient, expressive teacher, making this feel like a pairing that could quietly grow on everyone.

dancers.name: Jackson Olson
dancers.knownFor: Savannah Bananas • Banana Ball • social media
dancers.danceBackground: Athletic showman — frequent choreographed routines with the Savannah Bananas
dancers.bio: Jackson plays for the Savannah Bananas, where baseball comes with dancing, comedy and plenty of crowd interaction. He is used to learning choreography, being playful and performing without embarrassment—all valuable qualities on this show. Emma should be able to turn that natural showmanship into something extremely fun.
dancers.preseasonUpdate: One of the clearest preseason risers at roughly 13% in the prediction market. His built-in showmanship and comfort with choreographed crowd entertainment are making him a popular breakout pick.

dancers.name: Sarah Jane Nader
dancers.danceBackground: No formal dance background publicly established
dancers.bio: Sarah Jane is a model and reality personality from Love Thy Nader, as well as the sister of former DWTS contestant Brooks Nader. She brings poise, camera confidence and the excitement of being a true ballroom beginner. Newly promoted pro Hailey Bills gets a fresh slate and a partner who should look completely at home under the lights.

dancers.name: Connor Wood
dancers.knownFor: Comedian • TikTok • Brooke and Connor podcast
dancers.danceBackground: No formal training established — stage comfort and comic performance
dancers.bio: Connor is a comedian, social creator and co-host of Brooke and Connor Make a Podcast. He does not arrive with a formal dance résumé, but he knows how to entertain a room and laugh through an awkward moment—both very useful on DWTS. Rylee's upbeat energy makes this pairing feel instantly likable.

dancers.name: Conner Leavitt
dancers.knownFor: The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives
dancers.danceBackground: No formal training established — close exposure through wife Whitney Leavitt's DWTS run
dancers.bio: Conner is known from The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives and has already watched the DWTS experience up close through his wife Whitney's run. He is not coming in as a trained ballroom dancer, which leaves room for a real beginner-to-performer story. Adele, fresh from winning The Next Pro, will be making her mark right alongside him.
dancers.preseasonUpdate: His résumé still lacks formal ballroom training, but he does have casual social-media dance familiarity. That slightly upgrades the coordination outlook without putting him in the trained-dancer tier.

dancers.name: Giada De Laurentiis
dancers.danceBackground: No formal dance background publicly established
dancers.bio: Giada has spent years making complicated recipes feel approachable on television, and now she gets to be the beginner. The Emmy-winning chef and author is comfortable performing live but has no major dance background to lean on. With Alan teaching her—and a sore toe already testing her resolve—her attitude and improvement could win people over.
dancers.preseasonUpdate: Giada reported a bruised, swollen middle toe and expects to lose the toenail. She remains in the competition and described it as part of the process, but footwork comfort is now a genuine premiere-week concern.

dancers.name: Guillermo Rodriguez
dancers.danceBackground: No formal dance background publicly established
dancers.bio: Guillermo went from working security at Jimmy Kimmel Live! to becoming one of late night's most recognizable and lovable personalities. He may not have dance training, but he has comic timing, confidence and an audience that already enjoys watching him have fun. Reigning champion Witney has a chance to create the season's happiest crowd-pleasing routines.

notes: Auction draft: Sunday, Sept. 13 at 6 PM Central, two days before the Sept. 15 premiere.
